contentCheck.notes: Crop shows the full instructions, example and situations (a)-(h). Legacy reaction-prediction format: write reactants and products in net ionic form; students answer any five.

primary.evidence: Must write Zn + Ni2+ -> Zn2+ + Ni, omitting spectator nitrate ions.

supporting.evidence: Must recognize a single-replacement redox reaction to predict the products.

primary.evidence: Must recall that Al(OH)3 dissolves in concentrated OH- to form the complex ion Al(OH)4-, which is beyond AP reaction-type reasoning.
Must recognize combustion of a hydrocarbon to predict CO2 and H2O as products.
Must write CaCO3(s) and molecular CH3COOH reacting to give Ca2+, CH3COO-, CO2 and H2O, keeping solid and weak acid un-ionized.

supporting.evidence: Must recognize acetic acid as a weak acid so it is written as molecules, not ions.

primary.evidence: Must recognize a direct combination (redox) of Li with N2 to predict a nitride product.

supporting.evidence: Must use Li+ and N3- charges to write the product formula Li3N.

primary.evidence: Must predict the Lewis acid-base adduct F3BNH3, which relies on Lewis acid-base chemistry not assessed in the current CED.
Must recall that SO3 acts as an acidic oxide and reacts with OH- to form sulfate (or hydrogen sulfate) and water.

supporting.evidence: Must represent NaOH as OH- ions and omit Na+ spectators.

primary.evidence: Must write Pb2+ + I- -> PbI2, omitting Mg2+ and NO3- spectators.

supporting.evidence: Must identify PbI2 as the precipitate since magnesium nitrate is soluble (nitrate rule).

uncertainty: Legacy 'write the reactants and products' format; parts b, f, g rely on descriptive chemistry outside the current CED. Part c also requires knowing ethyne is C2H2 (organic naming, tagged contextual).
